terra.problem: The explanation is generic, and the closing farm-talk line adds no Papa Dorin personality.
This repeats the garden answer without a distinctive voice or a laugh where one could fit.
The customer comparison and closing line are flat; the explanation has little of Papa Dorin's comic voice.
The last two sentences repeat that cattle are absent without adding a clear joke or insight.
The text says Ahab refused to eat, not that he had no appetite or that the palace was full of food.
The text does not say Ahab went quiet while lying with his face turned away.
The explanation is flat and repeats that an apology is absent rather than adding personality or insight.
A seal on a letter does not generally mean the letter carries the king's name. This passage says Jezebel used Ahab's seal and wrote in his name.
The text names the recipients but does not say the letters went nowhere else.
Nobody showing up in armor is an added detail; the text does not describe what the men wear.
The elders and nobles carried out the instructions, but the text does not say nobody objected to them.
Jezebel goes on to mention Naboth himself, including his refusal and his death.
Jezebel does bring up silver: she says Naboth refused to give Ahab the vineyard for silver.
The text does not say that no crowd is gathering.
The text identifies the place where dogs licked Naboth's blood, but does not say it was the very place where he died.
Saying Elijah does not take the bait suggests Ahab was trying to provoke him, a reason the text does not give.
Calling Jeroboam and Baasha earlier kings states a fact from outside this passage without a reference.
Ahab called Elijah his enemy earlier in the passage, but the text does not say it was a few moments before.
